game.text: Miami at Jacksonville, Sunday, October 26, 2014, 1 p.m. ET, EverBank Field
game.label: Game

attack.text: Miami's front has 16 sacks through six games, with Olivier Vernon and Cameron Wake setting the edges. Make that front defend the run, the keeper and the screen from related 12-personnel looks. Kevin O'Connell's wide-zone and movement-pass structure supplies the first picture; Ben Johnson's Counter, Power, condensed releases and complementary shifts supply the answer when Miami overplays it. Move Kelce and Lewis without changing the eleven. Locate Grimes and Delmas before testing the intermediate middle. Win third down with protection and spacing, not a succession of slow-developing shots.
attack.label: The matchup I am attacking

protect.text: Free edge rushes, a disguised pressure Cousins cannot identify, and a takeaway that gives Tannehill a short field. We converted one of eight third downs against Cleveland and gained 86 yards on the ground. On defense, do not repeat Cleveland's 32 first downs or 11 third-down conversions. Miller cannot reach the cutback untouched; Wallace cannot get a free vertical release; Clay and Gibson cannot own the easy catch at the marker. Donald's penetration must remain tied to a complete run fit and four connected rush lanes.
protect.label: What I must not give them

change_course.text: If Wake or Vernon defeats the protection help, use SCAT Stick, Spacing, Mesh, the Slow Screen and a protected Y-Cross before taking another long-set throw. If Miami squeezes wide zone, hit Counter or Inside Zone; if the box loads, shift Kelce out and use the access or crossing answer. If Tannehill escapes an interior rush or Miami converts short third downs, simplify the A-gap presentation, contain both edges and tighten coverage at the marker. If cornerback or left-guard availability changes, reset the job assignments before kickoff.
change_course.label: What would make me change course

contingency.text: Adams needs the October 20 clearance; otherwise Thielen moves to X, Hurns supplies the next receiver position and Hawkins remains the movable Z, with Gabriel the next relief. Bitonio is the intended left guard only if the October 22 clearance and protection work permit it; otherwise Lucas stays at left guard as he did against Cleveland, with Brewster the interior relief. Norwell remains out under his independent hold unless the medical staff explicitly releases it. Daryl Smith is projected out through October 31; Posluszny makes the front declaration, with Telvin Smith and Sio Moore completing the first linebacker group and Stanford next. Talib returns outside only with independent clearance; if he cannot go, Butler starts outside opposite an eligible Verner. Verner's October 20 restriction controls his work; if he cannot go, use the eligible Talib and Butler, then Ball outside if both are unavailable. Ball is the nickel for continuity; Bouye enters that rotation only after clearance and a clean exchange rehearsal. If the available corners cannot cover the normal nickel jobs, use the medically eligible defensive backs and simplify the coverage before setting the seven inactives.
contingency.label: If Adams, Bitonio, Norwell, Smith, Talib, Verner or Bouye cannot dress

coverage_units.text: Westhoff rebuilds coverage units from the final dressed defensive backs, linebackers and receivers. Phillips and Prosinski take safety and kicking relief where eligible; Butler and Ball may have expanded corner duties. No player under an independent hold takes a walkthrough or a game assignment without medical authorization. Dwight Lowery may begin the designated return practice window on October 20 if cleared, but is not eligible to play October 26. Donald remains a first-unit interior starter with Marks in base, Nickel and Dime; Miller is the heavier interior alternative, not Donald's replacement on passing downs.
coverage_units.label: Special coverage and substitution consequences

base_personnel.text: Start from 12 personnel with Kelce and Lewis attached, wing or shifted to a spread picture; rotate to 11 without announcing pass. Anderson remains the first back and presses the wide-zone and inside-zone track, with Jones-Drew available for Power, Counter, pass protection and four-minute work. No preset touch split. Adams, if cleared, is X; Thielen works H and Hawkins Z, with Hurns and Gabriel used according to the actual matchup and availability. Monroe and Johnson need help on the correct edge, not an automatic chip that removes a required route. Linsley owns the center point with Bitonio or Lucas at left guard according to the medical and practice checks.
base_personnel.label: Base personnel and roles

learn.text: Does Miami play Wake and Vernon upfield against the same Wing wide-zone and Boot picture? Does the front slant when Lewis moves? Will Grimes stay with Adams or remain to a side? Does Delmas insert into a Power fit or hold the post? Do Miami's linebackers travel or bump with Kelce's shift, and do they exchange the Mesh crossers? Which defender owns the back when we show a Slow Screen after a dropback? Let the answers select the return calls.
learn.label: The first things I want to learn

opening_approach.text: Begin with wide zone and quick-game distribution to force Miami to declare front strength and coverage leverage. Repeat the formation with Boot, then Power and Counter when the backside defender runs over the top. Mix Bunch Mesh, SOLID Y-Cross and the back screen into the same personnel sequence. Take a protected Power Pass only after a safety has actually attacked the run. Opening ideas are choices in priority order, not an unchangeable first-drive script.
opening_approach.label: Opening approach

third_down.text: Short: counted Power, Counter or Inside Zone with access only when the perimeter wins leverage. Medium: Stick, Spacing, Mesh, Drive and SOLID Y-Cross, all with the marker as the landmark. Long: Y-Cross, protected Dagger or Slow Screen after the rush declares. We were one for eight against Cleveland; first-down gains and third-down distances matter as much as the call.
third_down.label: Third down

backed_up.text: Wide Zone, Inside Zone, SCAT Stick or Spacing. Use the correct chip and escape route. No blind vertical, delayed screen into the goal line or gratuitous shift that risks a false start.
backed_up.label: Backed up

red_zone.text: High: Y-Cross, protected Power Pass after the run-fit trigger, or Boot when the edge chases. Low: Mesh, Snag, Power and Counter, with an identified free defender. Goal line: downhill run and one protected pass answer; finish the center-guard exchange before choosing the play.
red_zone.label: High red zone, low red zone, goal line

two_minute.text: HOLD 11 or 12 for Stick, Spacing, Drive, Mesh and Y-Cross; use PRESS only after the current eleven communicates properly. Cousins carries the protection point and immediate sideline/clock answer.
two_minute.label: Two-minute / hurry-up

four_minute.text: Run toward the soundest fit, protect the football and mix quick completion or a gated Boot when Miami packs the box. Know the field position, lead and remaining time before third down; prepare the fourth-down call under the standing rule instead of discovering it after a stop.
four_minute.label: Four-minute / protect a lead

sudden_change.text: Secure a first down before chasing a highlight. Power Pass or Boot only when the safety or edge has given the exact trigger; otherwise run the base concept or the back screen into an overaggressive rush.
sudden_change.label: Sudden change / shot opportunities

front.text: Under with Donald at the attacking interior 3-technique alongside Marks, Mincey and Andre Branch on the edges; move to Nickel Even against open formations and Bear for short yardage. Roy Miller is the heavy-run alternate. Posluszny makes the front call while Daryl Smith is out, with Telvin Smith and Sio Moore in the first linebacker group. Set force before pursuit and stay square against Lamar Miller's zone cutback. Donald's first job is to own his gap, then penetrate; Marks and the ends cannot chase inside and leave Tannehill a boot or scramble lane.
front.label: Base front and run fits

coverage.text: Show Spagnuolo's crowded pressure surface and Flores's late rotation, but earn both with clean assignments. Present the two A-gap threats and usually send four: Donald and Marks compress inside while the edges keep the cage. Rotate between 1 Robber, 3 Match, Quarters and Cover 6 according to release distribution. Put Wallace's deep stem first in the outside coverage count, Gibson's intermediate routes next, and Clay's seam, crossing release and flat work in the linebacker-safety exchange. Use a genuine fifth man with Fire 3 only when Tannehill's hot answer and the vacated zone are covered. With injured corners and Daryl Smith out, do not make complexity the objective.
coverage.label: Coverage and rush approach

discover.text: Does Samson Satele redirect the line when both A-gaps show pressure? Does Lamar Miller scan inside-out or release? Do Albert and James chase defensive-line movement or keep a firm edge? Does Tannehill take the immediate throw, climb past Donald or escape the edge? How does Wallace change splits; where does Gibson settle; does Clay stay to help or release through the middle? Record the answer before dialing a counter.
discover.label: What we need to discover early

matchups.text: Donald stays on the field for the meaningful interior pass-rush downs, aligned against Miami's actual guard and center protection rather than a fixed target picked on paper. Marks complements him, Mincey and Andre Branch preserve the edges. Posluszny declares the front; Telvin Smith and Sio Moore own run-fit, underneath and back-release duties with clear handoffs. Talib and Verner play outside only if cleared, with Butler the first outside relief. Ball is the initial nickel, Prosinski the sixth defensive back, Rambo and Trawick at safety. Do not demand repeated late man exchanges from a replacement secondary.
matchups.label: Individual matchups / roles changed

kicking.text: Hawkins remains the kick and punt returner, with Hurns available on the prepared punt-return alternative. Scobee, Anger and Kreiter own the operation. Miami already has a special-teams touchdown in six games; cover with sound lane spacing and vice, avoid a cheap return-lane penalty, and finish punt protection before releasing. Westhoff confirms the replacement coverage players after the corner and linebacker exams; no medically unavailable player is carried into the 46 on reputation.
kicking.label: Return, coverage and operation instructions

endgame.text: Skalaski gives me the score, clock, field position, distance and timeouts before every material fourth down; Tice has the first eligible call ready under the standing rule. Cleveland's two late failed tries in our own territory make the field-position cost explicit in every pregame scenario, even though the standing rule has not been changed. Preserve timeouts for possessions and must-have communication. The booth controls automatic reviews and reviews inside two minutes. Prepare Cousins for an urgent sideline throw and for protecting a lead without relying on a fourth-down conversion.
endgame.label: Timeouts, challenges and endgame

participation.text: October 20 reviews Adams, Talib and Verner; October 22 is the projected date for Bitonio and Bouye; October 23 reassesses Norwell and Daryl Smith. Medical clearance controls all reps. Lucas, Posluszny, Moore, Ball, Butler and the healthy receiver order take the corresponding first-unit work until a cleared player has both permission and enough correctly executed assignment work to return. Reconfirm the seven inactives, 46 dressed players and kicking assignments after the final medical communication.
participation.label: If a medical assessment changes participation

tradeoff.text: No new gadget installation, no extra unprotected vertical-shot period and no repeated exotic pressure package before the base checks hold. The Flea Flicker is off this week's prepared menu. Monday is review and walkthrough, Tuesday off, Wednesday through Friday helmets only, Saturday walkthrough; this plan does not represent those practices as already completed.
tradeoff.label: What leaves the practice menu to make room

staff.text: I call the offense and defense. Tice organizes the offensive menu and relays the situation; Bates owns Cousins's protection and hot-answer review. Crennel prepares the defensive pressures and transmits the call, with Posluszny declaring the front while Daryl Smith is out. Westhoff sets the kicking operation from the actual dressed eleven. Bring the Week 7 third-down and fourth-down film into the meeting with the exact down, distance and field position. Challenge an assignment with a better football answer, then rehearse the correction. The package must be executable by the available players, not only clever on the board.
staff.label: Staff instructions

public.label: Public position, if I am adding one

open_decisions.text: Medical clearance for Adams, Bitonio, Norwell, Smith, Talib, Verner and Bouye; final left-guard, linebacker and corner assignments; the legal 46 and coverage teams. The standing fourth-down rule remains in force unless I separately change it.
open_decisions.label: Other open decisions

ready.text: The October 20, 22 and 23 availability decisions, protection communication on both possible left guards, Posluszny's front calls, the corner and nickel exchange, Donald's run-fit/rush-lane work, and Westhoff's final game-day coverage list have been checked before October 26 kickoff.
ready.label: Ready to lock after

event.summary: Stone set his Week 8 Game Plan against Miami: the call sheet frozen with 20 offensive calls and 19 defensive calls, fourth downs his standing rule, two-point tries his standing rule, kickoffs his standing rule; the 7 inactives Andrew Norwell, Daryl Smith, Jordan Poyer, Charles Leno Jr., Kasim Edebali, Hakeem Nicks, Todd Davis; OL order: Eugene Monroe, Joel Bitonio, Corey Linsley, Trai Turner, Lane Johnson, Cornelius Lucas, Mike Brewster, Charles Leno Jr., Andrew Norwell; LB order: Paul Posluszny, Telvin Smith, Sio Moore, Julian Stanford, Christian Jones, Todd Davis, Daryl Smith.
